title: SpaceX Poised to Launch Starshield Spy Fleet and Starship's First Orbital Test, While Google Sends AI Chips to Space
subhead: A consequential weekend for orbital power: SpaceX launches classified military satellites designed to outnumber anti-satellite weapons, Starship attempts its first full orbital flight, and Google begins testing TPUs in low Earth orbit as the AI infrastructure race goes extraterrestrial.

sections.heading: SpaceX Launches Classified Starshield Satellites for Space Force
sections.body:
SpaceX is scheduled to launch the USSF-385 mission from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Saturday, September 26, carrying classified Starshield spy satellites for the U.S. Space Force. The launch window opens at 4:56 a.m. PT, with a Falcon 9 flying a southeastern trajectory. This is the third classified Space Force mission from Vandenberg this month alone.

According to spaceflight outlets reporting on the mission, USSF-385 will deliver a batch of military satellites to low Earth orbit, part of a broader Space Force strategy to build a distributed constellation of reconnaissance platforms too numerous for adversaries to disable with anti-satellite weapons. The approach reflects a shift from small numbers of exquisite, multi-billion-dollar spy satellites to large constellations of cheaper, mass-produced spacecraft, leveraging SpaceX's high launch cadence.

USA Today reports that the mission underscores Vandenberg's growing role as a national security spaceport, with SpaceX conducting its sixth launch from the California base in September alone.
sections.whyItMatters: The USSF-385 launch reflects the Pentagon's pivot to constellation-based orbital resilience, betting that distributed satellites launched at high frequency by commercial providers can survive anti-satellite attacks better than traditional legacy systems.

sections.heading: Starship's First Fully Orbital Flight Set for September 28
sections.body:
SpaceX has scheduled Flight 14 of its Starship vehicle for September 28, 2026, marking the first time the program will attempt a full orbital flight. The company completed a wet dress rehearsal this week, confirming the vehicle is flight-ready.

According to SpaceX and spaceflight news outlets, the upcoming launch will carry 26 next-generation Starlink satellites into orbit, a major step up from previous suborbital test flights that carried no operational payloads. The Starship upper stage will circle Earth six times before splashing down in the Pacific Ocean, while the Super Heavy booster will attempt a splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico approximately seven minutes after liftoff.

This will be the third mission of Starship's Version 3, which debuted on Flight 12. The successful completion of an orbital flight with a commercial payload would mark a turning point for the program, transforming Starship from an experimental vehicle into a potential operational heavy-lift platform.
sections.whyItMatters: Starship's first orbital flight with 26 Starlink satellites would validate the vehicle's heavy-lift capability and begin unlocking the launch economics that underpin SpaceX's next-generation constellation plans, putting competitive pressure on every other launch provider globally.

sections.heading: Google Tests AI Chips in Orbit With Project Suncatcher
sections.body:
Google announced on September 24 that it is preparing to launch its first prototype satellite under Project Suncatcher, a research initiative testing whether AI computing infrastructure can operate in space. The launch is scheduled for the coming week as part of SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission, developed in partnership with satellite operator Planet.

According to Google's published update, the prototype will evaluate how its Trillium Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) perform under the physical stresses of launch, radiation exposure, and thermal extremes in low Earth orbit. Engineers at Google conducted vibration tests simulating launch forces up to 100 times Earth's gravity and proton-beam radiation testing at UC Davis's Crocker Nuclear Laboratory, reporting that the TPUs withstood radiation doses exceeding what they would receive over a five-year mission.

The long-term vision is ambitious: constellations of satellites carrying dozens of TPU chips each, connected by high-bandwidth laser communications, forming distributed AI data centers in orbit. Google cites a key energy advantage, as satellites in low Earth orbit can access near-constant sunlight generating up to eight times more solar power than comparable systems on Earth. The company plans a two-satellite orbital test of laser interconnects in 2027.

The initiative faces significant engineering hurdles, particularly in thermal management, as the vacuum of space eliminates air-based heat transfer. Google is testing heat pipe and radiator combinations as cooling solutions.
sections.whyItMatters: Project Suncatcher is the first serious attempt to move AI compute infrastructure off Earth, testing whether the convergence of cheap launch, abundant solar energy, and ruggedized processors can make orbital data centers viable for AI training and inference.

sections.heading: Nscale Raises $3.36B as Neocloud Competition Intensifies
sections.body:
London-based AI cloud company Nscale announced on September 25 that it has raised $3.36 billion in pre-IPO convertible financing, led by Third Point, with NVIDIA committing $1 billion of the total. The round included Apollo, Citadel, Hudson Bay Capital, Abu Dhabi Investment Council, and 8090 Industries, bringing Nscale's total capital raised to over $7 billion.

According to Unite.AI and HPCwire, the financing consists of an initial $2.36 billion tranche at closing, with NVIDIA's additional $1 billion expected in mid-November. The notes convert automatically into ordinary shares upon completion of Nscale's planned IPO on the New York Stock Exchange. Goldman Sachs acted as placement agent.

Nscale, founded in 2024 by Australian entrepreneur Josh Payne, operates a vertically integrated model spanning behind-the-meter power plants, liquid-cooled data centers, and large-scale GPU clusters. The company reports $103 billion in total contracted value, including a deal with robotics startup Figure to deploy up to 100,000 GPUs worth up to $6 billion.

The neocloud sector has seen a funding frenzy: Crusoe closed a $3.9 billion Series F at a $30.9 billion valuation, FluidStack raised $1.5 billion at an $18 billion valuation, and CoreWeave received a $2 billion follow-on from NVIDIA. In South Korea, Naver partnered with Brookfield and NVIDIA on a $10 billion AI factory in Sejong. Nscale differentiates itself by leveraging Europe's cheaper renewable power and government AI sovereignty push.
sections.whyItMatters: NVIDIA's expanding equity commitments to neoclouds reveal a deliberate strategy to fund the buildout of GPU demand outside the hyperscaler oligopoly, ensuring its hardware has enough buyers and deployment venues to sustain revenue growth.

sections.heading: Trump-Xi Summit: No AI Agreement, Only Acknowledged Differences
sections.body:
The Trump-Xi state visit concluded on September 25 with no binding AI agreement and no breakthrough on chip export controls. According to The Diplomat and Latin Times reporting, both governments rejected calls to slow AI development, and a proposed emergency channel for reporting AI-related security incidents remains under negotiation, not finalized.

Trump opened the talks by signaling little interest in new AI rules, having previously dismissed safety concerns as a 'hoax' on Truth Social. Xi took a different posture, calling for AI to be kept 'under human control' and urging both countries to 'jointly prevent the misuse and abuse of AI.' But Beijing's position comes with conditions: Chinese officials want relief from U.S. chip export controls addressed in parallel and will not accept limits on China's AI industry as a precondition.

The state dinner guest list revealed an open split in Silicon Valley. OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk backed Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call for external safety evaluations of catastrophic AI risks. Meta's Mark Zuckerberg and NVIDIA's Jensen Huang argued the risks are overstated. Anthropic's Amodei was notably absent from the dinner, a signal attributed to his hardline stance on China AI access and his company's legal clashes with the Trump administration over autonomous weapons and surveillance use cases.

China Daily, in a piece published September 26, framed AI cooperation as essential despite rivalry, noting that Chinese open-source models like Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 are now influencing U.S. market technology choices. Beijing announced the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization in July with 38 members, while Washington's State Department has been pressing signatories of its AI Opportunity Statement not to join competing initiatives.
sections.whyItMatters: The summit confirmed that AI governance between the two powers is stalled, with neither side willing to constrain its own development pace, leaving industry-led safety efforts as the only active track while export controls remain the primary battleground.

sections.heading: FBI Disrupts Chinese State-Linked Hacking Platform; NZ Names China Top Cyber Threat
sections.body:
The Justice Department announced on September 24 that it had seized internet domains tied to two Chinese state-linked hacking platforms known as QScan and QTRouter, operated by a group identified as QTFY. According to Time and Tickle the Wire, the FBI said the platforms helped Chinese actors hide the origin of attacks targeting NASA, the Federal Reserve, the Senate, the Departments of Energy, Justice, and Health and Human Services, as well as hospitals, telecom companies, and defense contractors.

FBI Director Kash Patel said the platforms were used to 'hide the origin of their attacks.' An FBI affidavit identified members of QTFY as former members of China's People's Liberation Army who used military relationships to secure contracts for offensive cyber operations through Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology Company. No arrests or charges were announced. The Chinese Embassy in Washington rejected the allegations.

Separately, New Zealand's National Cyber Security Centre released its annual Cyber Threat Report on September 25, identifying China as 'the most persistent and capable state actor undertaking cyber activity in New Zealand.' The report found that 86 of 369 nationally significant cyber incidents in the year to June 2026 had suspected links to state-sponsored actors, with activity targeting government agencies, health and education organizations, and IT managed-service providers. New Zealand's security agency had previously reported in August that China was the only country detected conducting espionage 'at scale' in the country.

A Pew Research report also flagged rising cyberattacks on U.S. municipal water systems, with a Utah audit revealing intrusions tied to Iran, adding a second state actor to the infrastructure threat picture.
sections.whyItMatters: The FBI domain seizure and New Zealand's public naming confirm that state-sponsored cyber espionage campaigns are expanding in scope and geographic reach, targeting critical infrastructure across multiple sectors with increasing brazenness.

sections.heading: US-Nigeria Mining Framework and India's Lithium Push in Zimbabwe
sections.body:
Nigeria and the United States signed a framework agreement on September 24 to deepen American investment in Nigeria's $700 billion solid minerals sector, according to Reuters. The agreement, signed on the margins of the UN General Assembly in New York, covers geological data sharing, mineral exploration, and processing cooperation. Nigeria's Solid Minerals Minister Dele Alake framed the deal as a bet on local value addition rather than raw ore export.

Meanwhile, Indian critical-minerals company Lohum disclosed plans to invest $100 million in Zimbabwe's lithium sector after securing rights to 10 mining blocks estimated to contain 30-40 million tonnes of lithium-bearing ore. According to Reuters and Business Insider Africa, Lohum has already shipped its first lithium ore from Zimbabwe and plans to process material into lithium sulphate locally before refining it into lithium carbonate in India.

The investment gives India a foothold in Africa's largest lithium-producing country, where Chinese companies, including Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt and Sinomine Resource Group, have invested approximately $2 billion since 2021. Zimbabwe supplied about 15% of China's lithium-concentrate imports in 2025. Lohum's entry will not immediately displace Chinese players but provides India with a direct mineral source for its battery manufacturing ambitions.

The moves come as KoBold Metals, a U.S. mining startup, is also using AI to search for critical minerals in the Democratic Republic of Congo, signaling a broader Western and allied push to diversify critical mineral supply chains away from Chinese dominance.
sections.whyItMatters: The US-Nigeria framework and India's Zimbabwe lithium push represent the most concrete steps yet by non-Chinese actors to build alternative critical mineral supply chains in Africa, though both face deep structural disadvantages against entrenched Chinese investment.

bottomLine: A consequential weekend for space and AI infrastructure: SpaceX is launching classified military satellites today and attempting Starship's first orbital flight on Monday, while Google begins testing AI processors in orbit, signaling that the competition for compute and orbital power is moving beyond Earth. On the ground, the neocloud funding race hit a new peak with Nscale's $3.36 billion round, the Trump-Xi summit produced no AI governance breakthrough, and the FBI disrupted a Chinese state-linked hacking platform targeting U.S. government agencies while New Zealand publicly named China as its top cyber threat. The critical minerals competition in Africa intensified with a US-Nigeria mining framework and India's $100 million lithium investment in Zimbabwe, both challenging but not yet displacing Chinese dominance.
sources: USA Today, SpaceX, Google Project Suncatcher update, Unite.AI, HPCwire, WowTale, The Diplomat, Latin Times, FirstPost, China Daily, Time, Tickle the Wire, Astro Awani, Blockonomi, The Register, Reuters, Business Insider Africa, Zimbabwe Situation, Pew Research
